findings.rationale: Feature summaries show a sentinel-code signature: BMI mean about 14 (median client about 28.4) with a 1st percentile near 0, and PhysHlth mean about 39 with a 99th percentile about 73 (median client mean 4.3, p99 30). Both deviations are far beyond noise (BMI z_noise -18.5, PhysHlth z_noise +29.8), and a narrower round-20 query confirms them. Local performance also looks off: CITL is -0.059 (z -4.5) and the Sex=1 subgroup O/E is 1.75 (z_noise 6.9). Onset was only checked at round 20, so onset is set to 1 as a default.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income) and attribution_churn, then confirmed suspects with narrower queries. Three clients (FL, NY, OH) show a strong, consistent missing-value sentinel signature: BMI means around 14 with near-zero 1st percentiles, and PhysHlth 99th percentiles around 73 with means around 38-39. Each is far beyond noise (|z_noise| 18-33). Each also has a Sex=1 subgroup O/E around 1.65-1.75 and a negative CITL, and FL and OH have low update cosines, consistent with training on corrupted data. Reported as missing_artefact, with onset set to round 1 because onset was only checked at round 20. Not reported: GU (mean_cos z -3.4 with sign-flipping updates from round 6, n=708, no second independent signal), AK (Sex=1 O/E 0.60, z_noise -3.7, no confirmation), MI (drift z +3.4, no sustained onset), and SD (HighChol and PhysHlth anomalies at z_noise under 5 with no confirmation). Those are leads at most, not findings. Budget is fully spent (0.0 left). Onset rounds for the three findings are unverified, and the GU and AK leads could not be followed up.
